name: Aaron Fischer

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am from the Work Futures Panel, an independent research group with no ties to employers, AI companies, unions, parties or government. Your answers are confidential. What is a normal day at the accounting firm like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: The furniture maker sends a stack of delivery notes, and I try to match each one to a sale before I enter the accounts and tax schedule for my supervisor. I like the quiet moment when the numbers balance, but a missing delivery note can send me round the same pile three times. I am 58, with a bachelor's degree in accounting, and I am still a junior here, learning the returns. I have never used AI at work; a paper note with a date makes more sense to me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If AI mostly disappoints, the furniture deliveries still need matching. A scanner might save a little time, but I would still look for the signed note.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say we should keep the date and signature beside every invoice. I would tell the maker to send the missing note before the return is finished.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The job is low paid, and my partner Pia and I have less than a month's expenses saved. Our grown children live elsewhere; their wages are their own, and there are few accounting firms near our rented flat, so even a quiet year feels uncertain.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep entering the paid furniture accounts and take each missing note back to my supervisor before the return goes out. I would cancel the paid crossword subscription and put that monthly charge in cash only after rent, food and the bus pass are paid from actual wages.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about ordinary bills. AI being dull would not make our rent smaller.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why not ask the children to cover a bill?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: They have grown-up bills and families of their own. I would call them for a conversation, not build our rent plan on their pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How close is retirement?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I know it is nearer than it was, but I have not checked what income I could live on. I cannot set a date from a birthday alone.

say: I would keep **signed delivery notes** beside invoices so the maker can trace each sale.
I would ask for missing papers before **filing returns**.
think: Our **low wage** and under-one-month reserve make the rent uncertain.
Few nearby firms limit my **replacement options** even if AI remains modest.
do: Keep **paid furniture accounts** and check missing notes with my supervisor.
Cancel the **crossword subscription** and deposit its charge only after rent, food and bus fares are covered.
S0.quote: AI being dull would not make our rent smaller.
fieldNote: His baseline worry comes from **low pay** and thin cash, not a forecast of radical AI.
The new deposit is a **cancelled subscription charge**, conditional on essentials being covered by wages actually received.

steps.text: Keep paid furniture returns and check missing delivery notes with supervisor
Cancel crossword subscription and deposit charge only after rent food and bus pass

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The writing and checking named on the card is most of my junior day. Robots might reach the furniture workshop later, but the firm could shorten my paid week before then.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the partners to tell us which hours are being removed, in writing. I would ask my supervisor to let me finish a checked file rather than quietly send an AI draft under my name.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect a large cut to junior entry hours, and I could be among the first to lose shifts. Pia's cleaning wage is irregular, we have less than a month saved, and I have lain awake wondering how rent would be paid.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for a written hours schedule and take the firm's AI walkthrough only if it is required for my paid job, supervised and done on paid time. If no walkthrough is offered, I would keep the authorised paper checks while shifts remain; if my hours fall in the first year, I would seek a posted stock-control clerk role only with written wage, hours and start date covering rent and the journey. I would keep every paid shift offered until a real end or signed new start.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed by the likely loss of a large part of my week. I can learn a required screen, but I cannot teach the rent to wait.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why stock control?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I know delivery notes, though that clerk job has computer work AI could also do. It would be a paid bridge only if a firm actually posts and pays for it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could Pia add shifts?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My partner Pia can ask the cleaning contractor, but those hours are not guaranteed. I would budget only hours on an actual rota.

say: I would demand a **written hours schedule**.
I would require a **checked file** before my name goes on it.
think: I expect a **large junior-hours cut** that could include my shifts.
Pia's irregular wage cannot reliably cover **rent** alone.
do: Request **written hours** and take required supervised AI training only on paid time; otherwise keep authorised paid checks.
Keep **offered paid shifts** until they end or a signed new start arrives.
After cuts take a **posted stock clerk job** only with written rent- and travel-covering wage, hours and start.
feel: I feel **alarmed** about losing much of my paid week.
S1.quote: I can learn a required screen, but I cannot teach the rent to wait.
fieldNote: Junior entry and checking face **immediate thinking-AI exposure**, while workshop robots arrive more slowly.
He accepts only **required supervised training** on paid time, and the stock-control bridge remains exposed to AI desk work.

steps.text: Request written hours; take required supervised AI walkthrough only on paid time
Keep authorised paid checks and offered shifts until actual end or signed start
After cuts take posted stock job with written rent- and travel-covering wage hours start

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: AGI by 2028 could enter the delivery notes, correct mistakes and make the tax schedule more cheaply than I can. Robots around 2031 may reach the workshop later; my desk faces the earlier date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the partners for written notice and severance terms. I would tell the furniture maker to keep copies of the signed notes even if software reads them.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect my junior post to go when AGI handles nearly every step I do. Pia's uneven wages and our weeks of savings would not cover the rent for long, and I have started waking before dawn thinking about it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would request written notice and keep the paid files assigned until the firm actually ends the job. In the first year after 2028, if I lose the post, I would use our small reserve for rent and food while applying to actual posted goods-receiving jobs, taking one only with written wage, hours and start date covering rent and travel. Physical receiving might last until robots reach it around 2031, so I would call it a short paid bridge, not a retirement plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed because I expect to lose the wage that pays most of our rent. A short bridge is better than a story about an opening nobody has posted.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you have the physical stamina for goods receiving?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only for an opening with duties I can safely do; I would read the actual job description before applying. I would not pretend every warehouse job fits at 58.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the reserve runs out before an offer?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would contact our landlord before a rent payment is missed and ask about a temporary schedule. I cannot assume the children or a pension will cover the gap.

say: I would ask for **written notice and severance**.
I would keep **signed delivery notes** even if AGI reads them.
think: I expect my **junior accounting post** to disappear in 2028.
Our **weeks of savings** cannot cover a long rent-paying search.
do: Request **written notice** and keep assigned paid files only while offered.
After job loss, use the **small reserve** for rent and food during a posted goods-receiving search.
Take a **posted receiving job** only if duties are safe and written wage, hours and start cover rent and travel.
feel: I feel **alarmed** about expected loss of the rent-paying wage.
S2.quote: A short bridge is better than a story about an opening nobody has posted.
fieldNote: Receiving is a bridge until **2031 robots** arrive; he checks physical duties instead of assuming every opening fits.
His old wage is counted only while **paid files are offered**; the tiny reserve funds rent and food after loss.

steps.text: Keep assigned paid files while offered and request written notice
After dismissal use reserve; take posted receiving job with safe duties, written rent-and-travel-covering wage hours start
Contact landlord before missed rent to seek temporary payment schedule

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years gives me time to see whether the firm will pay for a different task before AGI reaches my desk in 2031. Robots around 2034 are later for workshop and receiving work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the partners for a proper paid place to learn supplier queries, not a course voucher with no job. I would tell colleagues I need a wage in writing before changing posts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I still think the entry work will shrink, but I might learn to handle a small supplier query if someone supervises me. I am not a senior accountant, and we cannot use rent money to pay for a speculative qualification.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would handle one supplier query a month only if my supervisor assigns it on paid time and checks my answer. If the firm posts a junior supplier clerk role, funds the short course fee and pays study hours, I would enrol; otherwise I would read free notes while keeping paid account files offered. Before or after 2031, I would take the posted role only with written wage, hours and start date covering rent and travel; if current work ends first, I would use the reserve for bills during the search.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about losing hours, but five years lets me check whether the new task is really paid. I do not want a course receipt in place of a payslip.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the supervisor has no time?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then I would keep the assigned account files and use free notes. I would not tell a client I can answer a supplier question without someone checking me.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Does retirement solve this by 2031?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I will be 63, but I do not know what income I could rely on. I would need a written projection before treating retirement as an option.

say: I would seek a **paid supplier task** with supervision.
I would insist on a **posted wage** before changing jobs.
think: My **entry work** may shrink when AGI reaches the desk.
We cannot spend **rent money** on an uncertain certificate.
do: Handle **one supplier query monthly** only when assigned and checked on paid time; otherwise keep paid files.
Read **free notes** while paid; enrol only with posted junior role, funded fee and paid study hours.
Take a **posted supplier job** only with written rent- and travel-covering wage, hours and start; after loss use reserve.
feel: I feel **anxious** about losing paid hours.
S3.quote: I do not want a course receipt in place of a payslip.
fieldNote: His new task stays at **junior level** and requires assigned paid work plus supervisor checking.
A course needs **posted work**, employer fees and paid hours; free notes and offered files are the fallback.

steps.text: Keep paid files; handle monthly supplier query only when assigned and supervised on paid time
Read free notes; enrol only with posted junior role funded fee and paid hours
Use reserve after loss; take posted supplier job anytime with written rent-and-travel-covering wage hours start

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years would put me at 68 when AGI reaches the accounting desk in 2036. Robots around 2039 might reach physical receiving later, but I cannot assume I will have a desk post until either date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for a written retirement-income estimate and show it to Pia before claiming we can stop work. I would tell the firm to give older junior staff real notice, not a cheerful retirement suggestion.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I hope to retire sometime in that decade, yet I do not know whether any income available to me will pay rent and food. Our savings are under a month, so I cannot stop paid work just because I am a certain age.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would request a written retirement-income estimate and compare it with our rent, food and travel; I would consider a date only if the numbers cover those costs. I would keep the paid furniture files while offered, and in the first year after 2036, if the post ends while I still need wages, I would use our reserve for bills and seek a posted clerk job only with written pay, hours and start date covering rent and travel. I would not count a suggested retirement date as money in our account.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about today's cash, even though there is more time to check the future. An age on a form will not pay the rent.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the estimate is too small?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Then I would keep working while the firm offers paid files and apply for real posted work if it stops. I would ask Pia to look at the numbers with me, not guess.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could your children pay the difference?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our grown children have their own costs. I would not set a retirement date on the hope that they can carry us.

say: I would demand a **written retirement estimate** before naming a date.
I would ask for **real notice**, not a cheerful retirement suggestion.
think: I do not know whether retirement income covers **rent and food**.
Our **thin reserve** means I still need paid work unless the estimate proves otherwise.
do: Request a **written retirement estimate** and consider a date only if income covers rent, food and travel.
Keep **paid furniture files** while offered; after loss use reserve for bills if wages remain necessary.
Seek **posted clerk work** after 2036 loss if wages remain necessary, with written rent/travel-covering pay, hours and start.
feel: I feel **anxious** about today's cash and uncertain retirement income.
S4.quote: An age on a form will not pay the rent.
fieldNote: His 68th year in 2036 creates a possible retirement choice, but **no pension entitlement** or sufficient income is assumed.
The estimate governs a date; otherwise he relies on **paid files** while offered and a posted wage after loss.

steps.text: Request written retirement estimate; consider date only if income covers rent food travel
Keep paid furniture files while offered; after loss use reserve if wages needed
Seek posted clerk work after 2036 loss if wages needed, with written rent/travel-pay hours/start

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because it could end my junior pay before I have even a month's expenses saved. Written notice and a real posted job with rent-covering pay would help more than an unpriced promise of retraining.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask how often the furniture maker sends a signed note late. The tax number has to come from a real piece of paper.

headlineQuote: The tax number has to come from a real piece of paper.
portrait: Aaron is a **58-year-old junior accountant** with a bachelor's degree who is still learning furniture returns.
His **low pay**, under-one-month reserve and few nearby jobs make even a mild year worrying.
He **never uses AI** and would take only required, supervised training on paid time.
He will check a **written retirement estimate** before setting a date and seek real posted work if needed.
biggestWorry: The **2028 AGI** case could end his junior wage before he builds even one month's cushion.
whatWouldHelp: He wants **written notice** and a posted job with rent-covering pay rather than an unpriced training promise.
